explanation: Return an empty list for a missing subtree, a one-node list for a leaf, or concatenate the left subtree’s leaf list with the right subtree’s leaf list. Return references to the original leaves.
timeComplexity: O(nh) upper bound, O(n²) worst case: list concatenation copies every subtree’s leaves; a comb-shaped tree repeats many copies. A balanced tree takes O(n log n). Append-based versions visit each node once; Python’s returned-list concatenation adds repeated copying of descendant leaf lists.
spaceComplexity: O(n+h) peak auxiliary/output list and recursion storage; concatenations create temporary lists. Append variants use height-sized recursion plus one output per leaf; Python also creates temporary concatenated lists.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/tree_connect_leaves.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: The base cases contain exactly the appropriate leaves. At an internal node, all left-subtree leaves precede all right-subtree leaves; concatenating the two correct lists therefore produces the complete left-to-right list.
walkthrough: For [16, 7, 25, 2, 11, null, 30, null, 4], the leftmost leaf is 4 beneath node 2. Next comes leaf 11, then leaf 30 in the right subtree. Internal nodes 16, 7, 2 and 25 are not appended. Return [4, 11, 30]. The callable returns nodes and the wrapper extracts their data. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: A null tree has no leaves.
A one-node tree contributes its root as a leaf.
Different leaves with equal Data values are both retained.
